newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola completes integration of ex rebels into army.
newsitem.headline: Angola completes integration of ex rebels into army.

text.p: Angola's Armed Forces chief Joao de Matos on Thursday officially closed the process of integrating former rebel UNITA soldiers into a single national army, the state news agency Angop said.

The formation of a new Angolan army was one of the main aims of a 1994 peace agreement between the Luanda government and UNITA (the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola) to end 20 years of civil war.

Both factions agreed in negotiations last year to integrate a total of 26,300 UNITA soldiers into a single armed force. But Angop reported that by Thursday just 11,000 former rebels had joined the new Angolan Armed Forces (FAA).

Angop said Thursday's ceremony in Luanda, was witnessed by United Nations special envoy to Angola, Alioune Blonin Beye and ambassadors from the three observer countries, Portugal, Russia and the United States.
Nine UNITA generals have been absorbed into the national army in a process which began in exactly a year ago.
UNITA, which joined the government of national unity in April, however complained it was having difficulties persuading its fighters to join the FAA.
Armed soldiers caught outside the new system will from now be considered bandits.

More than 60,000 former rebel soldiers were disarmed at United Nations-supervised assembly camps around the country since 1996, where they had the choice to be integrated into the new army or demobilised.

Many UNITA soldiers, still awaiting demobilisation, deserted the camps after government forces attacked UNITA-held areas in the diamond-rich northeast in May in efforts to extend control over the entire countryside.
The government has accused UNITA of not disbanding its entire guerrilla force.
